The following patch adds perf_event support for the Xeon-Phi
PMU
column2: as documented in the ""Intel Xeon Phi Coprocessor (codename:

column1: Knights Corner) Performance Monitoring Units"" manual.
Even though it is a co-processor
column2: a Phi runs a full Linux

column1: environment and can support performance counters.
This is just barebones support
column2: it does not add support for

column1: interesting new features such as the SPFLT intruction that
allows starting/stopping events without entering the kernel.
The PMU internally is just like that of an original Pentium
a ""P6-like"" MSR interface is provided.  The interface is
different enough from a real P6 that it's not easy (or
practical) to re-use the code in  perf_event_p6.c
